messages:
elaine: Heads-up — we've got a streaming tail-latency regression after the last release. 95/99p for SSE streams (tool-calls that touch KV) jumped ~2.4x in CI perf. Affects hosted and dedicated perf tests. Rolling hold? :eyes:

miguel: Ack. I ran a quick profile on a repro load. Flamegraph points to two hotspots: the eventsource writer coalescing path and serializer marshal copying during toolcall frames. Lots of tiny socket writes piling up.

perf-bot: [perf/streaming-latency CI] job streaming-90pct failed: baseline 38ms -> 92ms (99p). Regression introduced between commits abc123..def456. See: https://ci.internal/reports/streaming-latency/262000

sam: Thanks, perf-bot. I'll start a bisect across the release merge. Suspects: PR#4521 (write coalesce changes) and PR#4519 (kvcache prefetch eviction tweak).

natalie: My quick thought: the write coalescing reduced syscall overhead but may be increasing micro-batching delay (Nagle-like). For SSE we care about flush boundaries per chunk. Also kvcache prefetch window bump could cause transient eviction churn, increasing cold lookups concurrently with streaming work.

miguel: Reproducer commands I used:
```
wrk -t12 -c100 -d60s --sse /v1/stream?model=xlarge
strace -e write -p <pid>
```
You can see clumps of writes delayed by ~3-8ms each before they flush. The serializer path shows an extra copy when toolcall metadata is present.

sam: Bisect update: narrowed to PR#4521 (write coalescing) as the primary cause. Reverting that change locally returns 99p to baseline in my run. PR#4519 amplifies the effect but is not the root cause.

elaine: OK — placing rollout hold on release. Can we get a minimal patch that keeps syscall savings but guarantees chunk flush at toolcall boundaries? Also please check kvcache prefetch window to avoid simultaneous eviction spikes during high fanout.

miguel: Plan: 1) open revert PR for the coalescing heuristic to stop the rollout gap, 2) a targeted fix that uses time-based coalesce with a very small max latency (configurable, default 1ms) and explicit flush after toolcall frame boundaries, 3) reduce kvcache prefetch window by 20% as a short-term mitigation. I'll open PRs in the next hour.

sam: Quick experiment idea: toggle TCP_NODELAY for the eventsource socket in staging to confirm Nagle-like behavior is the cause (no code-gen, just run change in runtime config). If latency drops, we can prefer explicit flushes over changing global socket options.

miguel: Did the staging toggle: enabling TCP_NODELAY dropped 99p by ~45% in a short run. So it's definitely coalesce-delay related, not purely serializer copies. Revert PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/4592 (revert of PR#4521). Also opening: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/4593 (coalesce-with-max-latency + flush-after-toolcall).

ci-bot: [PR 4592] CI perf job streaming-latency: PASS (99p within 5% of baseline).

elaine: Nice work — thanks. Hold remains until PR 4592 is merged and we validate longer runs. After merge, let's run canary rollout with the coalesce max-latency flag enabled for 5% of traffic and the kvcache prefetch reduction.

natalie: Will follow up with a short postmortem doc outlining the interaction (write coalescing + kvcache churn -> increased tail on SSE toolcall-heavy streams) and add a perf test that exercises toolcall+kv hot paths.

elaine: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
